rt.projectTitle: Reproject the source textures onto the result
rt.chartsTitle: Atlas islands: one colour per UV island
rt.deviationTitle: Deviation from the original model: blue to red
rt.opaqueTitle: Force the surface opaque, so the wireframe stops going through it
rt.xrayTitle: X-ray: see the far face through the near one
rt.abSplit: Draggable curtain: source left, result right
rt.abGhost: Ghost: the source in transparency over the result
rt.abNoneTitle: Nothing: hide both the source and the result
rt.peekTitle: Hold to see the source, release for the result (X)
rt.method: Method — pick one of the two
rt.decimateTitle: Spend the budget where the silhouette needs it
rt.rebuildTitle: Rebuild towards even edges and a valence of six
rt.scopeVisibleTitle: Only what is not hidden in the Scene tab
rt.scopePickedTitle: Only what is selected in the Scene tab
rt.devScaleHint: A multiplier on the run's own worst deviation, not an absolute distance: « how far did it move » only means something against how far it could have moved. At 1 the hottest colour lands exactly on the worst vertex; below that the ramp saturates and the merely bad areas join the worst ones, which is how you find them.
rt.maxDevHint: The second stopping condition, and the one that counts when you are after a quality rather than a budget: decimation stops when the next merge would move the surface by more than this. It is the difference between « make it 5,000 triangles » and « make it as small as possible without it showing ». At zero, only the budget decides.
rt.quadsHint: glTF has no quads, so the pairing travels beside the file as a diagonal mask, one integer per triangle.
rt.creaseHint: An edge folded more than the angle counts as a crease and resists. The seam cost protects UV borders, whose breaking shows in the texture long before it shows in the shape.
rt.smoothHint: Every pass is reprojected onto the source, otherwise a sphere deflates a little each time. This angle is not the one above, and that is deliberate: a mesh reduced fifty times is faceted everywhere, so the angle that means « crease » to a decimator means « the whole model » to a smoother.
rt.mapsHint: The reduced mesh still carries the original's UV layout, and past a certain point that layout no longer describes the surface it is laid on. The switch is in the bottom bar, beside the button whose cost it changes.
rt.mapsChoiceHint: Base colour alone is not enough: without metal and roughness the whole result inherits a single pair of scalars, and a brass buckle on a wooden handle comes back as matte wood. Emissive is dropped on its own when nothing emits.
rt.aoHint: Short, and only the crevices darken; long, and the whole silhouette shades itself. The sampling sequence is deterministic, so comparing two settings is not a guess.
rt.cageHint: A cage distance means nothing until you have seen the shell it describes: too short and the rays miss whatever sticks out of the reduced mesh; too long and they go and find the neighbouring part, and bake a door frame onto a door.
rt.atlasHint: These are two different things and both matter: the gap is empty space between the islands so no mip level blends them, the bleed is colour painted past each border so filtering never reaches the background.
rt.hintDecimate: Quadric error puts the triangles where the silhouette needs them, not evenly. That is what a static prop wants.
rt.hintIsotropic: Edges of equal length and a valence of six, which gives predictable loops around a joint. That is what a model about to deform or subdivide wants, and it is also what quad pairing needs.
rt.nothingToCompare: Nothing to compare until there is a result
rt.rebakeTitle: Redo the maps only, without touching the geometry
rt.rebakeNeedsResult: You need a result before you can bake it
rt.noBridge: No native bridge: opened outside the application.
rt.readsDirectly: The engine will read the original file directly.
rt.willExport: The scene will be exported to glTF before it is read, which takes a moment on a large model.
rt.scopeHintPicked: {n} item selected: one low poly per mesh.
rt.scopeHintPickedN: {n} items selected in the Scene tab.
rt.scopeHintPickedNone: Nothing selected: the whole scene goes through, one mesh at a time.
rt.scopeHintVisibleNone: No material hidden: the scope changes nothing.
rt.nothingToRun: No mesh to work on: everything is hidden.
rt.settingsMoved: The settings are in the bar's menu, over the model, so they are changed while looking at it.
rt.toolOff: No brush: the pointer turns the camera (Esc)
rt.toolDensity: Density: where triangles are worth spending. Alt, the eraser end or the barrel button take it away
rt.toolRegion: Region: the only part this run may modify
rt.toolGuide: Guide: draw a fold to hold, or a direction for the loops to follow
rt.paintViewTitle: Show what is painted on the model
rt.paintClear: Wipe everything: density, freeze, region and guides
rt.brushHint: Shift + wheel resizes it without looking away from the model. Alt, the barrel button or the eraser end reverse the stroke. The brush measures along the surface, so it does not go through a thin wall or jump to the next finger.
rt.guideHint: A fold is a promise: the result will still have an edge there. A flow says which way the loops should run, so the edges along it are kept and the ones across it are the ones to spend.
rt.influence: What the engine makes of it
rt.usePaint: Read the painting on the next run
rt.usePaintHint: Unchecked, the run ignores everything painted without erasing it: it is the only way to see what the painting actually changed, by comparing two results rather than a result and a memory.
rt.paintIntro: Four brushes, in the bar above the model. What they leave is not one more setting: it is what you know about the model and a triangle budget cannot guess.
rt.paintNothing: Nothing painted yet: the run behaves exactly as it did before.
rt.paintIgnored: The painting is there but the next run ignores it, as asked in the Paint tab.
rt.paintRegionOn: A region is painted: the rest of the model comes back unchanged, vertex for vertex. The triangle percentage is spent inside the region.
rt.paintReady: The next run will read all of it.
rt.patchHint: Paint the area to redo, change what needs changing — the cage first — and bake again: the rest of the texture does not move a byte. It only means something on a result that has already been baked, and the report says so: “Texels retouched”.
rt.symHint: The plane runs through the middle of the model and follows its own axes, not the room's: turning the model does not make the symmetry drift. The mirrored stroke is traced from its own surface rather than copied, so it stays on the model even where the model is not perfectly symmetric.
rt.toolClone: Clone: Alt-click to set the source, then paint to copy the texture over a defect
rt.cloneNeedsSource: Alt-click somewhere on the model to say where to copy from, then paint.
rt.cloneNeedsTexture: This mesh has no texture to retouch: it needs a bake first.
rt.cloneReady: Source set. Every stroke starts copying from it again. The clone only touches base colour.
